docker-run-compose-converter.assumptionNote: Only common run flags are converted; -d becomes docker compose up -d instead of a compose key.
benefits: Turns a working docker run command into a repeatable compose file in seconds.
Parses real-world commands: quoted values, --flag=value form, and combined short flags.
Repeated -p, -e, and -v flags each become proper YAML list entries.
The service name comes from --name, or is derived from the image name.

faqs.a: Paste the command into the input box. The tool tokenizes it, extracts the flags, and builds a services block. Copy the YAML or download docker-compose.yml, then run docker compose up -d.
faqs.q: How do I convert my docker run command?

faqs.a: It becomes the service name. If you omit --name, the tool derives one from the image — for example node:20-alpine becomes the service node.
-it, --rm, --privileged, and similar runtime-only flags are skipped because compose has no equivalent. Detached mode (-d) becomes docker compose up -d when you run the file.
Yes. Everything after the image name is treated as the container command and emitted as the command: key, so docker run ubuntu bash becomes command: bash.
faqs.q: Does it handle the command after the image?

faqs.a: The tokenizer respects single quotes, double quotes, and backslash escapes, so -e "API_KEY=abc 123" keeps its space. Extremely unusual shell syntax may still fail.
faqs.q: Does it handle quoted values with spaces?

faqs.a: Each -e becomes an environment list entry and each --env-file becomes an env_file entry. Both can be used together in the same command.
faqs.q: What is the difference between -e and --env-file handling?

docker-run-compose-converter.formula:
docker run [flags] IMAGE [CMD]
  --name N      ->  services: { N: }
  -p H:C        ->  ports: ["H:C"]
  -e K=V        ->  environment: ["K=V"]
  -v H:C        ->  volumes: ["H:C"]
  --restart R   ->  restart: R
  CMD after image -> command: CMD
howTo: Paste your docker run command into the input box.
Check the parsed summary: service name, image, and flag count.
Copy the output or download docker-compose.yml.
Run docker compose up -d with the file.
keyFacts: docker run flags map almost one-to-one to compose service keys.
-p becomes ports, -e becomes environment, -v becomes volumes.
Everything after the image name is the container command.
--name sets the compose service name; without it, the image name is used.
Multi-line commands with backslash continuations are handled automatically.
docker-run-compose-converter.keywords: docker run to compose, docker run to docker-compose.yml, convert docker run command, docker compose from run

labels.errorInvalid: Could not parse a docker run command. Check the command and try again.

limitations: Runtime-only flags (-it, --rm, --privileged) have no compose equivalent and are skipped.
Build-related flags do not apply to run commands and are not handled.
Unusual shell expansions like $(...) are not evaluated.

docker-run-compose-converter.quickAnswer: Developers prototype with long docker run commands, then need the same setup saved as a compose file for the team. This tool parses the run command — name, ports, environment, volumes, restart policy, and the trailing command — and generates the equivalent docker-compose.yml.
docker-run-compose-converter.tagline: Paste a docker run command, get a ready docker-compose.yml.
docker-run-compose-converter.workedExample:
Input:
docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 -e NODE_ENV=production -v /data:/data --restart unless-stopped nginx:1.25

Parsed: service web, image nginx:1.25, 1 port, 1 env var, 1 volume, restart unless-stopped.

Output (docker-compose.yml):
services:
  web:
    image: "nginx:1.25"
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    environment:
      - "NODE_ENV=production"
    volumes:
      - "/data:/data"
    restart: unless-stopped

Save and run docker compose up -d — the -d flag becomes the up command option.
